content.stem: A change in the 2021 edition of ISO 9712 separates radiographic techniques into:

Single-wall and double-wall radiographic projection only

Wall technique is a different distinction from film versus digital.
content.explanation: The 2021 edition splits film (RT-F) and digital (RT-D) techniques and treats image interpretation as its own technique.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, phased array ultrasonics is handled as:
options: The UT-PA technique, an extension of UT certification
A standalone NDT method with its own dedicated training table
A surface method like MT or PT
distractors: Phased array is a technique under UT, not a separate method.
Phased array is ultrasonic, not radiographic.
Phased array is a volumetric ultrasonic technique.
content.explanation: ISO 9712 treats phased array as the UT-PA technique under ultrasonic testing, covered through Annex F, rather than as a separate method.

content.stem: ISO 9712 UT-PA Level 2 certification requires the candidate to first hold:
distractors: The prerequisite is ultrasonic, not radiographic.
A general Level 1 does not qualify for UT-PA Level 2.
No Level 3 endorsement gates the technique; UT Level 2 does.
content.explanation: The phased array technique builds on conventional ultrasonics, so UT-PA Level 2 requires UT Level 2 certification as a prerequisite.

content.stem: Beyond the base UT requirement, ISO 9712 certification bodies set UT-PA training that is:
options: Already considered covered by the base UT training
Waived entirely for UT Level 2 holders
Additional, specific to the phased array technique
The same as TOFD in every case
distractors: UT-PA adds its own technique training beyond the base.
Holding UT Level 2 is the prerequisite, not a waiver of PA training.
Phased array and TOFD carry their own technique hours.
content.explanation: UT-PA carries additional technique-specific training set by the certification body; CGSB, for example, requires 70 hours beyond UT Level 2.

content.stem: Beyond UT Level 2, ISO 9712 UT-PA experience is:
options: Considered already satisfied entirely by the UT Level 2 hours
Additional experience specific to the phased array technique
distractors: UT-PA adds its own technique experience beyond UT Level 2.
Additional technique experience does apply.
It covers performing the technique, not interpretation alone.
content.explanation: UT-PA requires additional technique-specific experience over UT Level 2; CGSB sets this at 45 days, around 315 hours.

content.stem: An ISO 9712 phased array qualification limited to interpreting results carries training that is:
options: Reduced from the full technique requirement
Increased beyond the full technique requirement
distractors: Interpretation-only scope reduces, rather than increases, the hours.
The interpretation scope is set against the phased array technique hours.
Interpretation-limited qualifications are allowed.
content.explanation: Interpretation-only phased array qualifications carry reduced training, commonly half of the full technique hours.

content.stem: For an ISO 9712 phased array candidate, the conventional UT certification follows:
options: The standard UT training and experience tables
distractors: Phased array has no separate base table; it extends UT.
The underlying UT certification is fully required.
UT is a volumetric method, not a surface one.
content.explanation: Phased array sits on top of conventional ultrasonics, so the underlying UT certification still follows the UT entries in Tables 2 and 3.
